mermaid:
flowchart TD
  subgraph DSL["DSL de requetes"]
    REQ["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/ElasticRequest.scala"]
    QRY["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/ElasticQuery.scala"]
    AGG["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/ElasticAggregation.scala"]
  end
  subgraph Execution["Execution"]
    ES["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/Elasticsearch.scala"]
    EXE["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/executor/Executor.scala"]
    HTTP["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/executor/HttpExecutor.scala"]
  end
  subgraph Resultat["Reponses"]
    HITS["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/executor/response/Hits.scala"]
    RES["modules/library/src/main/scala/zio/elasticsearch/result/ElasticResult.scala"]
  end
  EXA["modules/example/src/main/scala/example/Main.scala"]
  QRY --> REQ
  AGG --> REQ
  REQ --> ES
  ES --> EXE --> HTTP
  HTTP --> HITS --> RES
  EXA --> ES
explication: Les requêtes, requêtes de recherche et agrégations sont construites avec un DSL typé, puis soumises à la couche Elasticsearch. HttpExecutor envoie l'appel HTTP et les réponses sont transformées en ElasticResult, comme le montre l'application d'exemple.
source: Claude, d'après l'arbre du dépôt et le README
explication_en: Queries, search queries and aggregations are built with a typed DSL, then submitted to the Elasticsearch layer. HttpExecutor sends the HTTP call and the responses are transformed into ElasticResult, as shown in the example application.
